Russia Unveils Jet-Powered BM-35 Drone With 217 Mph Speed — Russian propagandists released footage of an upgraded, jet-powered BM-35 attack drone. According to Ukrainian expert Serhii Beskrestnov, the Russians claim the drone can reach speeds exceeding 350 km/h (217 mph) and strike targets up to 200 kilometers (124 miles) away. The drone reportedly carries a 10-kilogram warhead and can be operated in first person view (FPV) mode, allegedly unaffected by electronic warfare.

Ukraine Tests Last Shadow T200 Interceptor Drone, Exceeding Expected Range — Ukrainian defense developer Ukrainska Bavovna has successfully tested the new “Last Shadow T200” interceptor drone, achieving a range of 122 kilometers (76 miles) during recent combat trials – well beyond the originally anticipated 70 kilometers (43 miles). The T200 is designed to defend against Russian Shahed, Geran, Gerbera, and Molniya drones, featuring a top speed of 300 km/h and an operational ceiling of 5 kilomete

Ukrainian Navy Strikes Russian Bastion Missile System in Crimea — The Ukrainian Navy reported striking the launch positions and deployment site of a Russian Bastion coastal missile system in occupied Crimea early morning Sunday, Aug. 16. The military stated the strike resulted in significant, though unspecified, losses to Russian weapons and personnel. The Bastion system is a scarce asset used by Russia to launch supersonic Onyx and hypersonic Zircon missiles at Ukrainian territory.

Poland Proposes European Legion With Ukrainian Veterans — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski advocated for the creation of a permanent “European Legion” during an interview with Ekathimerini. He suggested the force could recruit combat-experienced Ukrainian veterans post-war to bolster European defense capabilities. Sikorski emphasized that Europe must take greater responsibility for its security rather than relying solely on the US, while maintaining that the proposed force would complem

Gulf Allies Question US Ties Over Iran Conflict — US allies in the Persian Gulf, including Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar, are increasingly frustrated with US President Donald Trump’s diplomatic approach to the war with Iran. Regional officials cite unpredictable policy shifts and have begun questioning the necessity of hosting US military bases. The discontent follows a recent mutual defense pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, indicating a push to diversify security partnerships.

Russian Strikes Devastate Metinvest’s Zaporizhstal Factory, Epicentr Mall in Zaporizhzhia — Successive Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia have severely damaged Ukraine’s industrial and retail sectors. Overnight Aug. 10-11, a ballistic missile strike killed seven workers and forced a complete shutdown of Metinvest’s Zaporizhstal steel plant. Early on Aug. 12, a Russian strike destroyed an Epicentr shopping centre in a residential area, causing a massive fire.

‘No Room for Mistakes’: What Next for Protestors Demanding Fedorov’s Reinstatement? — The protests against Mykhailo Fedorov’s dismissal as minister of defense are increasingly expanding in focus, reflecting broader public concerns about corruption, non-transparent decision-making, and the government’s lack of accountability. Although a major rally is planned for Aug. 16, it remains unclear whether the protests will continue if Fedorov is not reinstated, especially as Fedorov himself has neither

Ukraine’s  Mahuchikh Wins Third Consecutive European High Jump Gold — Ukrainian athlete Yaroslava Mahuchikh won gold in the women’s high jump at the 2026 European Athletics Championships in Birmingham, England, clearing 1.97 meters on her first attempt. This marks her third consecutive European title following victories in 2022 and 2024. Poland’s Maria Zhodzik took silver and Montenegro’s Marija Vukovic won bronze, both clearing 1.95 meters. Fellow Ukrainian Iryna Herashchenko finished fifth wit

Drone Attacks Spark Large Fires at Wildberries Hubs Near Moscow — A large-scale drone attack on the Moscow region early Sunday morning resulted in massive fires at two major logistics centers: the 200,000-square-meter (77,200 square-feet) Wildberries facility in Koledino and the Severnoye Domodedovo complex. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin claimed air defenses downed 105 drones, while operations at Vnukovo, Domodedovo, and Zhukovsky airports were suspended. Separately, explosions were reported late

Russian Strikes on Kryvyi Rih and Kyiv Leave 2 Dead, 16 Injured — Russian forces launched combined ballistic missile and drone attacks on Kryvyi Rih and Kyiv early Sunday morning, Aug. 16. In Kryvyi Rih, strikes on industrial facilities left two people dead and 13 injured, while a separate attack in the Nikopol district injured another individual. In Kyiv, missile strikes caused fires and damage in the Obolonskyi and Holosiivskyi districts, injuring three people.

Ukraine War News Today - Top Stories and Breaking Updates from Kyiv Post — Stay informed with the most important Ukraine breaking news today. This page compiles the top headlines and critical updates from across Ukraine, offering a real-time snapshot of key developments. Whether it’s military updates, political changes, or international reactions — we bring you the latest Ukraine news as it happens. All reports are carefully curated from verified sources and KyivPost correspondents on the ground

Why Tehran Fears President Zelensky — Teheran is uneasy. Ukraine has a clear interest in imposing costs on Iran’s military network supporting Russia. Its target should be the Iranian regime’s military machinery.

Ukraine Claims Heavy Russian Losses, Successful Counteroffensive in South — Ukraine says July brought some of Russia’s heaviest personnel losses and record vehicle losses of the war. Ukrainian forces reportedly regained 745 square kilometers in the south through incremental attacks, while drone strikes disrupted Russian logistics.

Ukrainian Defense Firm DEMZ to Build Ammunition Plant in Lithuania — Lithuania’s Ministry of Economy and Innovation has signed an agreement with the Ukrainian defense company DEMZ to establish a new ammunition plant. The project will include a new facility in the Prienai district and an existing site in Alytus. Construction is scheduled to begin in autumn 2026, with production meeting NATO standards expected by late 2027. The ammunition will initially supply the Armed Forces of Ukraine, with pla

Poland Holds Largest Military Parade Amid Major Defense Buildup — Poland hosted its largest-ever military parade on Saturday to mark Armed Forces Day, featuring over 2,000 troops, 300 vehicles, and 60 aircraft in Warsaw, alongside a naval parade on the Baltic coast. Prime Minister Donald Tusk and President Karol Nawrocki emphasized the need for military strength to ensure deterrence. The event highlighted Poland’s rapid military modernization, including recent acquisitions of F-35 fighter jets a

Ukraine Condemns Russian Move to Erase Borders With Occupied Areas — The Ukrainian Ministry of Foreign Affairs has responded to Russian plans to abolish border control zones between Russian regions and occupied Ukrainian territories. The ministry stated that relocating checkpoints does not alter internationally recognized borders. Kyiv characterized the initiative as a political attempt to create the illusion that the seized territories are fully integrated into Russia.

World Archery Allows Russian Athletes to Compete Under National Flag — The World Archery Federation announced Friday that it has lifted restrictions on Russian athletes, allowing them to compete under their national flag and anthem at federation events. The decision follows a July 2026 ruling by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) that ended the suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee. Ukraine’s National Olympic Committee has appealed the IOC decision to the Court of Arbitration for Sp

HUR Cyber Specialists Attack Wildberries Digital Infrastructure — Cyber specialists from Ukraine’s Main Intelligence Directorate (HUR) attacked the digital infrastructure of Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries on Aug. 10-11. The cyberattack caused widespread disruptions to the company’s payment infrastructure and customer service channels. The incident follows a series of Ukrainian drone strikes on Wildberries warehouses, which analysts estimate have destroyed up to one-third of the company’s w

How Europe’s Political Center Lost Its Voters - Why Meloni, Le Pen, and the AfD Are No Longer on the Margins — Europe’s traditional political parties are losing voters as many citizens increasingly doubt their ability to address concerns about migration, economic security, living costs, and governance. The growing success of figures such as Meloni, Le Pen, and the AfD reflects declining trust in the political center rather than a simple shift toward extremism.

Russian Strikes Target Pavlohrad and Combine Harvester in Zaporizhzhia — Russian forces struck the city of Pavlohrad in the Dnipropetrovsk region, injuring two men and causing a fire. In a separate incident in the Zaporizhzhia region, an FPV drone attacked a combine harvester, injuring two agricultural workers. These attacks follow earlier strikes on Aug. 15 in Marhanets, which killed a three-month-old boy, and a drone attack on the city of Zaporizhzhia that damaged a shopping center and an indu

Europeans Seek Role in Ukraine Peace Talks Amid US Uncertainty — France, Germany, and the UK are collaborating on a joint format for Ukraine peace negotiations, concerned that Donald Trump’s administration might sideline them. European diplomats emphasized that the war’s outcome is too critical to European security to rely solely on the US. Meanwhile, President Volodymyr Zelensky is struggling to appoint a new ambassador to Washington following the dismissal of Olga Stefanishyna.

Poland-Ukraine High-Stakes Dispute Is Far From Over — Despite the worst being over, it is becoming increasingly difficult to find satisfactory solutions to Poland and Ukraine’s historical dispute. This means that the cost of resolving the crisis is rising.

Iran Rejects US Talks Resumption, Cites Violated Peace Agreement — Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi announced that Tehran has not decided to resume negotiations with the US, accusing Washington of violating the Islamabad memorandum intended to end the war. Araghchi noted that mediators from Qatar and Pakistan remain in contact but clarified this does not constitute formal talks. Separately, Iran is conducting technical discussions with Oman to define new maritime routes in the Strait of H

Zelensky Confirms Flamingo Missile Strikes Deep in Russian Territory — President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed on Saturday, Aug. 15, that Ukrainian forces used “Flamingo” missiles to strike the Progress Space Rocket Centre in Russia’s Samara region, 900 kilometers from the border. He also confirmed long-range attacks on the Savasleyka airfield, which hosts Russian missile carriers, and an oil facility in Ust-Luga. The confirmation follows earlier reports of explosions at the Samara aerospace indu

Russia Delays New Mobilization Wave Despite Rising Troop Losses — The Kremlin currently has no plans to initiate a new mobilization wave despite growing frontline losses and troop shortages. Sources indicate that Moscow is relying on financial incentives to recruit volunteers, although finding willing recruits is becoming increasingly difficult. Analysts note that a second mobilization could risk significant economic and social consequences in Russia. To delay a domestic draft, Moscow has report

Poland Refuses to Lift Ban on Ukrainian Grain, Citing Farmer Concerns — Polish Agriculture Minister Stefan Krajewski stated that Warsaw will not lift its unilateral ban on Ukrainian grain imports, despite ongoing pressure from the European Commission. Krajewski emphasized that the grain must be directed to third-country markets rather than remaining in Europe, and he expressed skepticism about increasing transit volumes through Poland without greater port capacity. The issue of Ukrainian agricul

Romania Reports Fourth Discovery of Drone Debris in 24 Hours — The Romanian Defense Ministry reported finding drone fragments in Plauru, Tulcea County, near the Ukrainian border, on Friday, Aug. 14. The incident marks the fourth such discovery in 24 hours, following findings near Luncavița and on the beaches of the Saturn and Costinești resorts. Earlier in the week, on Aug. 11, Romanian military divers destroyed two Russian-produced Gerbera-type drones found drifting near the Neptun Deep gas pro

Polish Police Detain Two Suspects Following Assault on Ukrainians — Polish authorities have detained two women in connection with an incident of aggressive behavior directed at Ukrainian citizens outside a pub in Poznań. The incident, which occurred on Aug. 13, was documented in a video showing the women shouting at and physically confronting the victims. Poland’s Interior Minister confirmed the arrests on Friday. The suspects, who were reportedly intoxicated, await a decision on formal charges.

Polish Pilecki Institute Websites Hacked With Russian Propaganda — Hackers breached the websites of the Witold Pilecki Institute in Poland, along with its branches in Berlin and Augustów, posting Russian propaganda and anti-Ukrainian narratives. The institute announced on Friday that its IT team blocked the overnight attack, took the sites offline, and secured the archives. A security review is currently underway. The incident follows a separate, massive cyber breach involving the medical record

Ukrainian Flamingo Missiles Target Samara Aerospace Plants in Russia — Ukrainian FP-5 “Flamingo” missiles struck industrial facilities in Samara, Russia, on Aug. 15. Following the attack, the chief designer of the Ukrainian defense company Fire Point published footage of a Flamingo missile launch. Open-source intelligence analysts identified the targeted site as the shared production zone of the Aviakor aviation plant and the Progress Space Rocket Centre. Russian officials confirmed localized in

Germany Urges Citizens to Avoid Ukraine Rail Travel Ahead of Aug. 24 — The German Embassy in Kyiv has issued a security advisory for its citizens to avoid rail travel in Ukraine ahead of the Aug. 24 Independence Day, citing the risk of Russian strikes on transport and energy infrastructure. The Ukrainian Center for Strategic Communications, referencing US intelligence, reported potential preparations for a large-scale attack on Kyiv’s energy sector. The warning follows an Aug. 13 Russian drone s

Trump Plans to Claim Strait of Hormuz as US Territory — US President Donald Trump stated on Friday, Aug. 14, that he intends to declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory upon the conclusion of the war with Iran, asserting that a US blockade currently controls the waterway. The announcement follows reports of two new attacks on ships in the strait and the collapse of ceasefire extension talks. Iran previously demanded the lifting of the US blockade and financial compensation to reopen the strai

Russian Drone Kills Baby in Marhanets High-Rise — Early Saturday morning, Aug. 15, Russian forces launched a drone attack on a high-rise residential building in Marhanets, Dnipropetrovsk region. The strike killed a three-month-old boy and injured 11 people, with seven hospitalized in critical condition. Separately, drones hit Zaporizhzhia, damaging a shopping center and an industrial enterprise. These attacks follow deadly strikes on Aug. 14 in the Donetsk and Cherkasy regions that killed at lea

Zelensky on Air Defense: ‘It Is Not Easy, but It Will All Happen’ — Zelensky says Ukraine will secure more air-defense missiles, Patriot systems and domestic production agreements, despite political delays that continue to cost lives.

Russia Admits New Petrol Shortages as Ukrainian Strikes Hit Refineries — Russian authorities acknowledge new petrol shortages as Ukrainian drone and missile strikes continue targeting the country’s refining capacity.

Zelensky Signals More Deep Strikes as Ukraine ‘Blocks Off Russia’s South’ — Ukraine is widening its “long-range sanctions” campaign against Russian energy, maritime and financial networks, with Zelensky signaling more strikes ahead.

Zelensky: Ukraine Expects 30,000 Russian Occupiers to Be ‘Eliminated’ in August — Ukraine is reinforcing the Sloviansk and Kostiantynivka directions as Zelensky sets a 30,000-troop August attrition target.

Vance Says Keeping Oil Prices Low Is US ‘Goal Number 1’ in Iran War — US Vice President JD Vance said affordable oil and gasoline now rank as the top US priority in the Iran war, ahead of preventing Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

Why Putin Chose the Kurils Now – and What It Means for Ukraine — Putin’s first visit to the disputed Kuril islands deepens tensions with Japan and shows how Moscow is linking its war against Ukraine to a broader confrontation in the Indo-Pacific.

US Backs Japan After Putin’s Visit to Disputed Kuril Islands — The US ambassador to Japan said Washington recognizes Tokyo’s sovereignty over islands visited by Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday, Aug. 13. Japan summoned Russia’s ambassador in response, while Moscow insisted the islands are part of Russian territory and not a matter for discussion with foreign states.

Ukraine’s International Register of Damage Opens 2 New Damage Claim Categories — The Register of Damage Caused by the Aggression of the Russian Federation against Ukraine (RD4U) opened two new claim categories on Thursday, Aug. 13, covering humanitarian expenditure and demining costs. The register currently consists of 23 categories, with 20 more planned, according to the presidential website.

Ukraine Sanctions 13 Vessels, 39 Entities Over Stolen Grain Exports — President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a decree Friday, Aug. 14, putting into effect a decision by Ukraine’s National Security and Defense Council from that same day. The new sanctions target 13 vessels, 11 Russian nationals and 28 companies involved in illegally exporting Ukrainian grain from occupied territories.

Former Navy SEAL Explains Russia’s Secret Campaign in Europe — In this deep-dive report for Kyiv Post, former US Navy SEAL Chuck Pfarrer breaks down Moscow’s hybrid warfare doctrine – from 2,000 unidentified drones probing NATO airbases and Telegram-recruited “single-use” sabotage agents, to state-sponsored assassinations in broad daylight.

Russian Soldier Sentenced to 12 Years for Raping Woman in Donetsk Region — The Prosecutor’s General Office announced that a Russian serviceman was sentenced to 12 years in prison for systematically raping a 57-year-old woman over two months, while his unit occupied a village in the Pokrovsk district. According to the prosecutors, the abuse ended in December 2025 when the serviceman was captured in combat by the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU).

Russian Mercenary Targets Ukrainian Artist in Warsaw — A Russian national allegedly recruited by Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) was plotting to assassinate Ukrainian rapper and blogger Kyivstoner in Warsaw. Polish authorities announced on Thursday, Aug. 13, that they detained the suspect on Aug. 7, before the attack could take place.

‘We’ll Warm Ourselves With the Fire of Russian Oil Refineries’: Ukraine Hits Back at Russia — Ukraine responded to a Russian post that appeared to threaten winter strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure by warning that Russian oil refineries could become targets that warm Ukrainians this winter.

‘They’re Starting to Moan’: Lavrov Threatens ‘Harsher’ Strikes — Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov rejected a ceasefire along the current front line and threatened “harsher” strikes against targets he claims support Ukraine’s military.

Putin Ordered Kremlin to ‘Destroy NATO and EU From Within’ – NYT — Moldova is emerging as a key target in Russia’s reported strategy to undermine NATO and the EU, with Western intelligence warning that Vladimir Putin could seek control of the country after Ukraine. Its strategic location, Russian troops in Transnistria, and energy vulnerabilities, make Moldova a potential launchpad for wider Kremlin aggression.

Zelensky Struggles to Find Ukraine’s Next Envoy to Trump — Ukraine is struggling to fill its ambassadorial post in Washington after Olga Stefanishyna’s dismissal, with potential candidates reluctant to take on a difficult role amid uncertainty over US policy toward Kyiv, Politico reports.

‘Only a Madman’ Would Say Sending Patriots to Ukraine Weakens Poland, Polish Minister Says — Poland has no plans yet to transfer Patriot batteries to Ukraine, Deputy Defense Minister Cezary Tomczyk said, dismissing opposition claims that such a move would leave Poland vulnerable. He argued that intercepting Russian missiles over Ukraine ultimately strengthens Poland’s security, calling the opposing argument “something only a madman would come up with.”

Mobilisation Rumours: Kremlin Under Pressure? — Russia is weighing a new mobilisation as its war effort stalls and economic pressures mount. Analysts warn it could deepen public discontent, strain Russia’s administrative system and worsen labour shortages. The Kremlin is seeking alternatives, including North Korean support, while European policymakers are urged to exploit growing tensions within Russia’s elite.

Exiled Putin Critic Says Push for Peace Put Him in Danger — Russian anti-war politician Boris Nadezhdin has fled to France after years of carefully calibrated criticism of the Kremlin. He says authorities finally crossed a line by threatening criminal charges, as growing war fatigue and calls for peace face ever harsher repression.

‘Like Snow on Your Head’: Russia Threatens Ukraine With Winter ‘Freeze’ as Kyiv Pushes for Ceasefire — Russia has threatened Ukraine with a winter “freeze,” appearing to signal more attacks as temperatures drop. The warning came just a day after Kyiv offered Moscow a mutual “freeze” on attacks against civilian targets in the Black Sea, amid escalating strikes on ports and maritime infrastructure.

Putin Has an Unexpected Ally in Ukraine’s War — Russia’s attacks are increasingly colliding with extreme heat and drought in Europe, putting pressure on Ukraine’s alternative trade, electricity, fire response and water systems, Newsweek reports.

Drone Shot Down in Latvian Airspace: Military — NATO fighter jets shot down a drone that strayed into Latvian airspace Friday, the latest sign of growing unease over drone activity across Europe. The incident came as Russia and Ukraine traded fresh drone strikes, with dozens of Ukrainian drones reportedly downed over Russia’s Leningrad region.

Russian Oil Refinery Shuts Down for Months After Ukrainian Drone Strike — A Russian oil refinery more than 1,300 kilometers from Ukraine has been completely shut down after a Ukrainian drone strike, with repairs potentially taking up to six months. The strike adds to Kyiv’s escalating campaign against Russia’s oil industry and a growing fuel crunch across the country.

Romania Starts Shutting Down Sole Working Nuclear Reactor — Romanian state-owned nuclear power producer Nuclearelectrica has started the process of disconnecting its sole working reactor from the power grid due to record low Danube river levels, it said on Thursday.

Ust-Luga Ablaze Again as 54 Ukrainian Drones Hit Russia’s Key Baltic Oil Port — Ukraine attacked Russia’s key Baltic oil port of Ust-Luga with 54 drones overnight on Aug. 14, triggering a fire and disrupting operations. The strike marks at least the sixth attack on the port this year as Kyiv intensifies efforts to hit Russia’s lucrative oil-export infrastructure.

The Danger of Empty Deterrence – the Lesson From Leipzig — Every Western security service, our militaries, and political leaders should be alarmed by the incident in Leipzig Airport, where an explosive-laden drone was positioned near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo aircraft.

‘Patriot Licenses for Ukraine are Not in America’s Interest’ | Stefan Korshak — “The Americans are not enthusiastic about arming Ukraine,” Stefan Korshak, Senior Defense Correspondent at the Kyiv Post, says in World Talks. According to him, granting Ukraine a license to produce Patriot systems would not be in the United States’ interest.

Ukraine Offers Russia Black Sea Moratorium — Ukraine has proposed a mutual halt to attacks on civilian ships and ports after striking Novorossiysk, as Russian attacks drive Ukrainian grain exports down 76%.
Russian Drone Attack Injures 3 in Cherkasy Region — Three people were injured after a Russian drone struck a residential building in the Smila community of Cherkasy region.

Putin’s New Clothes: Sinking Fleets, Staged Strength, Fear of Anti-War Millions — Putin’s military makeover comes as Russia faces naval setbacks, pressure on its shadow fleet, and signs that millions may support ending the war.

Russian Strikes Kill 1, Wound 15 in Kramatorsk as Civilian Toll Climbs — Russian strikes killed at least one person and wounded 15 in Kramatorsk, while a separate attack in Zaporizhzhia injured two more, including a child.

North Korea Threatens ‘Stronger Deterrence’ Ahead of US-South Korea Drills — North Korea threatened stronger deterrence measures as US-South Korea drills prepare forces for possible combat with troops hardened by fighting alongside Russia in Ukraine.
